anchors.note: Factual basis of the appraisal confirmed: r=0.92 is printed with df=4 in both the text and the Figure 3 caption, for 5 people (n−2=3). The printed p-values fit 3 df better (r=0.92 gives p≈0.027 with 3 df, 0.009 with 4), so the label is probably a misprint rather than a wrong analysis.
The 14-month figure (mean, SD 2) comes from Materials and Methods, Subjects, on the same page.

for_senior_author: Risk of bias (reader 2 agrees: very high): reader 2 adds the non-independence of the cross-sectional ANOVA (now reporting issue 4) as a further concern; decide whether it changes any domain judgment.

Interpretation gap (reader 2 agrees: substantial): reader 2 suggests adding that the title and summary call the change a recovery of a methamphetamine-induced loss (pp. 9414, 9418), which presupposes that early-abstinence DAT was drug-induced and that later values return toward a pre-use level; the design shows neither.
not_added: Methods give paired t tests (p. 9415) while the Figure 2 caption says repeated-measures ANOVA (p. 9416): confirmed; with two time points the tests are equivalent, so not added.
